title: ready-05: agent contract, agent status in the pane row, and sounds
summary: All four tasks DONE; 29/29 accepted. Claude native Waiting -> Working -> Error verified and explicitly accepted by Antonio for closure; successful Claude response unverified. Changes remain local; PR targets next.
description:
Decisions 13, 19, 20 in `~/projects/heca-pro/docs/decisions.md` (decision 13 now reads "Claude Code, Codex, pi and OpenCode", 2026-10-03). Replaces the status-and-sounds part of F008 (`agent-integration/agent-integration-plan.md`, P048 tasks T173 "Agent status display" and T175 "Transition sounds", both deferred) — reuse its research on hooks, rewrite the design against today's code. Rooms, orchestration and agent-comms are heca-pro, not here.

## Current state
- `heca-core/src/backend/terminal/osc.rs:4` — the escape-code reader knows only prompt start, command start, pre-exec, program, command finished, cwd.
- `heca-core/src/runtime.rs:72` — `PaneRuntime` has no agent state. Process status and pane rows: `heca/src/app/process_monitor.rs`, `heca/src/providers/workspaces/pane_row.rs`.

## Goal
- **One agent contract** any agent program implements: recognise it (by program), start it (with whatever it needs to report status), read its status. Claude Code, Codex, pi and OpenCode are built-in implementations of the same contract a plugin would write — code never branches on a program's name.
- Status set: working, waiting for input, waiting for permission, finished, error, compacting, subagent running — open to more.
- Status sources: Claude Code hooks printing a notification escape code (added through `--settings`, the user's own settings untouched), Codex's own notification codes, a small pi extension writing to a side channel, OpenCode (below). The reader learns notification codes (OSC 9 / 99 / 777).
- Agent line in the pane row: name, status, current task — composed from existing widgets, theme-driven.
- Sounds on status changes, configurable per status (and per project).
- Status changes are events (DOM-shaped event system) and appear on the socket's event stream.

## OpenCode facts (v2.0.19, from heca-pro, 2026-10-03; details in heca-pro docs/to-check.md items 5 and 6)
- Per-run set-up without touching the user's config: env `OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR` (a folder with plugins) or `OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT`, merged over the user's config.
- Status/events: its local server (default 127.0.0.1:4096) streams events at `GET /event`; plugins get bus events (e.g. `permission.asked`, `tool.execute.before`).
- Usage: each message stores tokens and cost (`~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db`, table `message`).
- Resume: `opencode --session <id>` / `--continue`.

## Preserve
- Non-agent panes unchanged; process status stays separate from agent status.
- AGENTS.md § 0; nothing hard-coded.

## Done when
- Claude Code in a pane shows working → waiting → finished in its pane row and plays the configured sound; the same for Codex, pi and OpenCode; a test agent added through the contract (as a plugin would) works the same.

## Verified implementation and remaining checks (restored 2026-10-24)
The shared contract and composed pane row are implemented and verified (T171/T173). Persistent integrations and the installer CLI are implemented, preserving user settings and native trust. Sound sources/defaults/configuration and background playback are implemented. The accepted persistent-installation decision supersedes the older temporary --settings setup above. Source references, review, native evidence and the remaining native Claude criterion are in .planner/docs/p102-closeout.md. Finish existing P102 work before recovery or other phases. PR targets next; no commit is authorized by this update.

Current closeout (2026-10-24): T171, T173 and T175 are DONE. T175 C5 passed with real native Pi and Antonio explicitly hearing the configured sound in the GPU app. T174 remains planned at 12/13; its C2 successful Claude native cycle is the only open check. Total: 28/29. The weekly quota prevented the last Claude success check; do not substitute a fixture or close that criterion without evidence. Current report: .planner/docs/p102-closeout.md. Preserve the current flash behavior. Changes remain local; PR targets next.

Final acceptance, 2026-10-24: Antonio explicitly accepted the real Claude Waiting -> Working -> Error quota-limited cycle in place of a successful model response. This supersedes the earlier pending-Claude statements above and narrows the original successful-cycle done-when requirement only for Claude. T174 C2 is now accepted; T174 is DONE (13/13). All four P102 tasks are DONE, total 29/29 accepted. Successful Claude response remains unverified; the error cycle and row flash were tested in the GPU app. See .planner/docs/p102-closeout.md and the phase acceptance decision. P099 transport remains separate work. No source changes, commits or push authorized.

tasks.title: Persistent agent integrations - install, inspect, update and uninstall
tasks.description:
Implement explicit, persistent agent integrations through the shared T171 contract. Built-in drivers cover Claude Code, Codex, pi and OpenCode; other programs use the same public registration API. Never branch on program names in the host.

Design authority: this task's Accepted Decision a1ebcc65-dfe9-456e-b95c-d5c07643a834 replaces the earlier temporary-launch setup described here and in P102. Reuse verified native API facts from agent-integration/agent-integration-plan.md, not its older setup design.

## User flow
The user explicitly chooses a program, for example `heca install integration codex`. Provide matching inspect, update and uninstall operations through one shared module. Nothing is installed automatically. The installed integration persists until removed and is inactive outside Heca. Once enabled, it reports for commands typed into existing Heca terminals and for Heca-launched programs. Per-session identity and reporting connections remain temporary; remove the competing per-launch hook/extension installation path.

## Delivery, settings and updates
Bundle integration files with the Heca release. Keep installed files in stable per-user locations appropriate to each program and use Heca's normal config for program/event choices. Preserve existing native settings, hooks and plugins; register and remove only Heca-owned entries. Keep native hook review/trust intact. Record integration versions and owned files/entries; inspection checks the actual installation, including modified or missing files. Update is explicit, preserves choices and detects local edits before replacement. Heca app updates supply newer assets without silently reinstalling integrations. Safe writes and recoverable changes are required. Event selection is separate from installation; sounds belong to T175 and remain off by default.

## Shared implementation and ownership
The installer is a machine-local filesystem operation and works without a session server. It must use the existing action/catalog conventions when exposed to app/plugin/RPC callers; it must not become another route for session mutations. A future settings page calls these same operations; building that page is outside this task.

P099/T544 (heca-dev2) owns CLI dispatch in heca/src/app/cli.rs and supplies the registration entry point. P102 owns the handler/shared module and does not edit P099's dispatch file. Coordinate the concrete handler signature before connecting it.

P099 owns heca/src/server/change.rs and T546 event/snapshot transport. P102 supplies serializable AgentState and agent transitions, including clearing state. Reuse the existing agent model, with previous/current values for transitions and current agent state in snapshots. No second wire model or parallel event store. Existing ServerWaker and serde work needs no installation changes.

## Verification and completion
Verify installation, repeat install, inspection, updates, removal, preservation of unrelated settings, edited files and native trust behavior. Exercise reports inside Heca through each built-in driver and an externally registered driver, and confirm installed integrations stay inactive outside Heca. Retain reusable work from T171 (contract), T173 (status line) and T175 (optional sounds); do not treat the temporary implementation as completion of this rework. Record native provider/account limitations separately from integration failures. Review with Opus before completion. PR targets next under F012 decision fa766c9f-b933-4b97-b626-9453265558a7. Do not commit without Antonio's request.

2026-10-24 recovered closeout: installer CLI is implemented and its four real-host tests pass in feat/p102-agent. P099 remains the owner of broader transport. See .planner/docs/p102-closeout.md. Successful Claude completion remains unverified because of the account quota.

---

Completed persistent integrations and shared install/inspect/update/uninstall operations, actual installer CLI, settings preservation/recovery, built-in and external-driver reporting, documentation and agreed review. Existing evidence: .planner/docs/p102-closeout.md; 2320 scoped tests passed excluding the documented unchanged focus_door scanner baseline, scoped Clippy -D warnings passed, four actual installer CLI tests passed. Fresh native GPU test on 2026-10-24: Claude Code v2.1.310 with installed hooks in target/p102/live-ui/native/.claude showed Waiting -> Working -> Error after "Reply with exactly OK. Do not use tools or change files."; weekly quota reset Oct 26 at 7am Europe/Rome. Antonio accepted native trust, confirmed row flash, and explicitly accepted this real error cycle for closure. The phase Accepted Decision records that C2 acceptance change; checklist now 13/13. Successful Claude response remains unverified and is not claimed. P099 broader socket transport remains separate ownership, not unfinished P102 work. No source edits, commits or push in this closeout. Existing implementation: heca/src/agent/, heca-core/src/agent/, heca/src/app/cli/, heca/tests/integration_cli.rs and heca/tests/agent_launch.rs in /Users/antonio/projects/heca-p102. PR targets next; changes remain local.

acceptedDecisions.title: Explicit persistent integration installation and P099 ownership boundary
acceptedDecisions.decision: Users explicitly install persistent integrations per registered agent program. Nothing is installed automatically. Persistent installation replaces per-launch hook or extension injection; session identity and the reporting connection remain temporary and active only inside Heca. Provide one shared implementation for install, inspect, update and uninstall, callable by the CLI and a future settings page. Preserve user settings, unrelated hooks and plugins, and native trust prompts. Sounds remain optional and off by default. Machine-local installation does not require a running session server; commands that change session state still go through the existing socket/action path. P099/T544 owns CLI dispatch; P102 owns the integration handler and shared operations. P099 owns server/change.rs and T546 transport; P102 supplies the serializable agent state and transition contract.
acceptedDecisions.rationale: Antonio agreed to replace temporary launch setup with explicit persistent installation, discussed using the same operations from a future GUI, and requested this task description/checklist update. The 2026-10-21 coordination proposal from heca-dev2 separates CLI and transport ownership from P102 installation work. Existing ServerWaker and serde work is unaffected. Restored after the canonical main planner reverted to an earlier branch snapshot; Antonio requested preserving P085/P035/F003 while recovering completed work.
acceptedDecisions.implementationNotes: Ship integration assets with Heca, record installed versions and owned entries/files, inspect actual files, and offer explicit updates without silently rewriting agent settings when Heca itself updates. Preserve user choices and detect edits before replacing owned content. Reuse the existing driver registration path; no closed list or program-name branches in the host. The future settings page is outside T174. P099 adds Change::PaneAgentChanged using the same PaneId, previous and agent fields as P102 ChromeEvent::PaneAgentChanged, with AgentState reused from heca-core; do not create a duplicate wire model. Refer to F012 branch decision fa766c9f-b933-4b97-b626-9453265558a7: PR targets next. This task decision supersedes older temporary-setup examples in T174 and P102 research; it does not change task status or ownership.

tasks.title: Sounds when an agent's status changes
tasks.description:
Depends on T171. Decision 19 in `~/projects/heca-pro/docs/decisions.md`.

Play a sound when an agent's status changes (not on every event). The audio runs on its own thread so the render loop never waits (`rodio` was the earlier choice — re-check). Configured in config.toml per status (enabled, volume, sound file), overridable per project (P101), off by default. Default sounds shipped. Sound is one channel of the notification settings per event (heca-pro decision 37) — build it so it fits that table, not as a separate system.
